bull.b: Minimal debt reduces solvency pressure and preserves more flexibility than a highly leveraged biotech would have. This balance-sheet profile can help Mereo direct available capital toward clinical development and partnerships while limiting interest and refinancing burdens.

The Sentynl arrangement supports Mereo’s partnership-based, capital-light strategy by creating potential non-dilutive economics around alvelestat. If the option is exercised and development succeeds, milestone and royalty participation could provide meaningful future funding without requiring Mereo to commercialize alone.

Alvelestat’s planned Phase 3 progression gives Mereo an advanced clinical asset tied to a defined rare-disease opportunity and unmet medical need. A later-stage program can improve partnering credibility and create clearer regulatory and commercial value than an early discovery pipeline.

bear.b: The absence of meaningful current revenue leaves Mereo dependent on future partnering, financing, or successful product commercialization to support operations. Persistent large losses also indicate that clinical progress has not yet translated into a self-sustaining earnings base.

Materially negative operating and free cash flow show that Mereo cannot currently fund its activities internally. Continued clinical investment therefore creates recurring financing needs, increasing exposure to dilution, funding timing, and the ability to secure favorable partner economics.

The extended minimum-bid-price deficiency remains a structural financing and visibility risk rather than a routine operating issue. Failure to regain compliance could threaten the Nasdaq listing, complicate investor access, and make future capital raising or partnerships more difficult.
